newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Air raid on Kabul kills 4, wounds 15.
newsitem.headline: Air raid on Kabul kills 4, wounds 15.

text.p: An air-raid on northeast Kabul by a lone plane on Sunday killed at least four people and wounded 15, including a United Nations employee, according to local hospitals.
The plane swooped low over the city and dropped four bombs on the residential district of Wazir Akbar Khan, destroying three houses including the office of the U.N.'s World Health Organisation.
Another bomb landed close to the outer wall of the United States Embassy, unused since 1989, destroying a five-yard (metre) section of it.
Shortly after the raid Taleban anti-aircraft gunners criss-crossed the sky with tracer fire, but did not appear to have hit the plane.
Taleban fighters commandeered cars to take the wounded to hospital in the absence of the city's ambulance service, a victim of five years of internecine warfare in the capital.
Frightened residents huddled in the gateways of their burnt-out houses as Taleban fighters searched for the dead and wounded among the rubble.
Roads around the site were strewn with smouldering debris, sheets of corrugated iron riddled by shrapnel and household items, including a shaving brush.
Forces opposing the Taleban have launched a number of air-raids on Kabul since suffering a defeat on the front line north of the city a week ago.
Sunday's raid came shortly after tens of thousands of Kabul residents gathered at four sites in the city to pray for rain at the request of Mullah Mohammed Omar, the leader of the Taleban.
The bombs landed approximately a mile from the site of the biggest gathering.

The Taleban, which captured Kabul in late September from the ousted government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani, has enforced a strict Islamic code in the more than two-thirds of Afghanistan under its control.
